tasks.short: Maintain customer charge and payment records and resolve allocation exceptions.

steps.what: Check approved charge batches against supporting invoices in the {ERP}.
Enter validated charges into customer accounts in the {ERP}.
Download transactions from the {BANK}.
Match receipts to open invoices and record allocations in the {ERP}.
Investigate ambiguous receipts through the {EMAIL} and propose supported corrections.
Approve and record nonstandard ledger adjustments in the {ERP}.
Copy balances and unresolved items into a tracking workbook in the {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to import approved charges, receive transactions from the {BANK}, and allocate payments using exact references and approved matching rules. Keep ambiguous items in an {ERP} exception queue with supporting evidence, supervisor approval for nonstandard adjustments, and a live balance view that replaces the duplicate tracker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing import and matching features were incompletely configured. Inconsistent references and unclear exception ownership encouraged manual re-entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Established import formats and matching rules handle routine records. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector and validation work without introducing a model into accounting decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Split payments, disputed invoices, duplicate receipts, and unexplained deductions need investigation. GDPR access and retention controls still apply; employee consultation depends on national rules and whether monitoring changes.
tasks.human_edge: Establish why money moved, distinguish a customer dispute from an allocation error, and support an adjustment with evidence.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of unresolved payment allocations by customer impact.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying transactions to resolving ambiguous receipts and preventing repeat errors. Posting and adjustment decision rights remain unchanged unless explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Explain whether a customer's payment has been received and allocated.
reach.learn: Read allocation states, distinguish receipt from settlement, and explain unresolved balances.

evidence.claim: Charge imports, exact payment matching, duplicate prevention, and exception queues are established deterministic patterns.
Exact documents order imports and stock synchronisation, supporting the integration pattern rather than proving payment reconciliation.
The step shares, remaining time, and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: The company uses the {ERP} as the customer accounting record.
The baseline includes manual batch handling and a small duplicate tracker; companies with configured matching already have less work to remove.
Only unambiguous, balanced matches post automatically; all other receipts enter the exception queue.
The build configures existing posting controls and does not replace the accounting ledger.
unknowns: Which charge imports, bank feeds, and matching features are already enabled?
What proportion of receipts have reliable invoice references?
Who may approve adjustments, and which thresholds apply?
Are interfaces, test accounts, and representative transaction samples available?
Does the change trigger employee consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Can existing {ERP} configuration replace custom integration entirely?
Which matching rules achieve acceptable precision on historical transactions?
How will retries, reversals, duplicate imports, and partial payments be tested?
new_work: Resolve the exception queue and monitor its age.
Maintain matching rules and customer reference mappings.
Review failed imports, duplicate alerts, and reconciliation totals.
Maintain access permissions and adjustment audit trails.
tasks.statement: Keep records of customers' charges and payments.

tasks.short: Assemble credit evidence, calculate financial indicators, and prepare a reasoned credit assessment.

steps.what: Retrieve customer balances and payment history from the {ERP}.
Assemble investigation reports and financial documents from the {DOCS}.
Read reports in the {DOCS} and extract relevant facts with source references.

loop.input: Indexed reports and financial documents for one applicant.
loop.output: Candidate facts with source passages, dates, units, and unresolved contradictions.
loop.check: Validate schema, applicant identity, source location, dates, and numerical consistency; an analyst verifies material facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document, capped at 30 documents per case; unreadable or larger packs go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields use direct mappings; variable narrative reports need bounded language extraction.

steps.what: Calculate ratios, exposure, and payment trends in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Assess repayment evidence, inconsistencies, and uncertainty against credit policy using the {DOCS}.
Write and approve a sourced assessment memo in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Analyst-authored conclusions, verified facts, calculated indicators, and an assessment template.
loop.output: A sourced memo expressing the analyst's conclusions and outstanding uncertainty.
loop.check: Check every figure against calculated data and every factual claim against evidence; the analyst approves the released memo.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, capped at 2,000 words; unresolved discrepancies return the template to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle fixed sections, but case-specific explanations need bounded drafting from human conclusions.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins authorised history from the {ERP} to an indexed evidence pack in the {DOCS}, then calculates indicators with versioned formulas. Bounded loops extract sourced facts and draft the analyst's conclusions into a memo; the analyst verifies material evidence and approves the assessment before it reaches the credit decision maker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence arrives in different formats and periods. Document interpretation, calculations, and credit judgment are often mixed in one manual process.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can produce constrained, source-linked fields, while ordinary code performs calculations and consistency checks. This improves preparation without requiring automated credit judgment.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence may be stale, contradictory, or incomplete, and ratios do not settle repayment capacity. GDPR decision safeguards and EU AI Act classification require review of the actual use; human review must have substance rather than merely endorse an automated score.
tasks.human_edge: Weigh contradictory evidence, understand unusual financial circumstances, and defend a proportionate assessment.

ambition.what: Weekly evidence freshness decisions for open credit applications.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing explanations and requesting decisive evidence, with less time assembling packs and formatting memos. Credit approval limits remain unchanged.

reach.task: Triage application backlogs by missing evidence and review complexity.
reach.learn: Distinguish a documentation delay from a material credit concern without treating queue priority as a credit decision.

evidence.claim: Rossum documents extraction, rule checks, and exception routing for order documents; this is an adjacent pattern, not validation of credit assessment.
The SCHUFA judgment shows that a score strongly relied upon by a lender can itself constitute an automated decision.
Deterministic calculations with human credit judgment are a plausible design; the proposed savings and build ranges remain estimates.

assumptions: The task produces an assessment, while final credit authorisation is a separate action.
The baseline mixes business credit cases with some individual applicants; personal-data safeguards apply where relevant.
Models extract facts and express human conclusions; they do not generate credit scores or recommend acceptance.
Build ranges cover a limited deployment under existing credit policy, not a new regulated scoring service.
Documents are available electronically and may lawfully be processed for the stated purpose.
unknowns: Are applicants individuals, businesses, or both?
Which document types, languages, currencies, and reporting periods occur?
Who verifies facts, signs assessments, and makes final credit decisions?
Does the intended implementation fall within EU AI Act high-risk creditworthiness provisions?
Which GDPR safeguards and national credit rules apply to the actual process?
What additional compliance, procurement, or consultation lead time is required?
research_questions: Which documents already provide structured exports that remove the need for extraction?
Can source-linked extraction reliably detect period, currency, and applicant mismatches?
What evidence must an analyst see to challenge a draft assessment effectively?
Which representative cases expose material errors before rollout?
new_work: Verify extracted facts and resolve conflicting sources.
Maintain formulas, templates, and evidence freshness rules.
Evaluate extraction errors across document formats and applicant groups.
Maintain source lineage, access controls, and model processing arrangements.
tasks.statement: Compile and analyze credit information gathered by investigation.

tasks.short: Request external credit information and handle reciprocal reference disclosures.

steps.what: Verify applicant identity, enquiry purpose, and permission against the case in the {CRM}.
Request and retrieve reports through a credit bureau service in {OTHER}.
Contact bank references through the {TELEPHONY} to clarify missing or conflicting information.
File reports and reference notes against the applicant in the {DOCS}.
Prepare a reciprocal reference using permitted account facts and a template in the {DOCS}.
Approve recipient, permission, and disclosed facts before releasing the reply through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A controlled connector on the {DATA_PLATFORM} submits approved enquiries to the credit bureau service in {OTHER}, records receipts, and files results in the {DOCS} against the {CRM} case. A fixed-field generator prepares reciprocal references from permitted account facts, and the {WORKFLOW} releases them through the {EMAIL} only after recipient and disclosure approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate service logins, licensing restrictions, identity mismatches, and unclear disclosure permissions prevented reliable straight-through handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Where licensed interfaces exist, connectors and fixed-field templates remove rekeying and copying. No language model is needed for standard requests or replies.
tasks.still_hard: Access rights do not establish a lawful purpose for every enquiry or disclosure. GDPR, contractual restrictions, and national confidentiality rules still require case-specific checks; informal references may remain unavailable or disputed.
tasks.human_edge: Establish whether a request is legitimate, resolve identity ambiguity, and decide what information may fairly and lawfully be shared.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving disputed or missing reference information and less time moving reports between records. Disclosure authority remains with the designated approver.

reach.task: Prepare factual reference replies and acknowledge correction requests.
reach.learn: Apply disclosure limits, verify recipients, and distinguish factual corrections from credit judgments.

evidence.claim: Licensed data retrieval, identity matching, request logging, and fixed-field replies can use deterministic integrations.
Rossum documents checked data transfer into business systems, supporting the integration pattern but not bureau access or reciprocal disclosure.
No digest source demonstrates this complete credit-reference workflow; feasibility, costs, and time estimates need local validation.

assumptions: The statement's 'potential creditors' means applicants or counterparties seeking credit; the intended population needs confirmation.
External credit information and reciprocal disclosures are distinct branches; shares represent a blended workload.
At least one external service offers a licensed interface or structured file exchange.
Reciprocal replies use approved factual fields, without free-text opinions or automatic disclosure.
The proposed correction-tracking service records progress and ownership; it does not alter external bureau data.
unknowns: Which external services are used, and what interface and redistribution rights are licensed?
What permits each enquiry and each reciprocal disclosure?
Which identifiers reliably distinguish applicants?
Which recipients, fields, and channels are approved for reference replies?
Who owns correction requests involving external providers?
What access, contracting, consultation, and retention requirements apply?
research_questions: Can existing {CRM} or {WORKFLOW} connectors handle the licensed service?
How should ambiguous identity matches be stopped before an external enquiry?
Can a fixed-field reply meet normal requests without narrative drafting?
Which service restrictions prevent automated filing or reuse?
new_work: Maintain service credentials, entitlements, and connector mappings.
Review failed requests and ambiguous identity matches.
Maintain disclosure field lists and recipient verification procedures.
Handle applicant correction requests and preserve enquiry and disclosure logs.
tasks.statement: Obtain information about potential creditors from banks, credit bureaus, and other credit services, and provide reciprocal information if requested.

tasks.short: Interview credit applicants to clarify financial circumstances and complete the credit evidence record.

steps.what: Review the application and prepare missing-data questions using the {DOCS}.
Arrange the interview through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}.
Verify identity and explain the interview purpose over the {TELEPHONY}.
Discuss income, obligations, and unclear evidence with the applicant over the {TELEPHONY}.
Write and verify the financial interview record in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Typed interview notes, existing application fields, and the interview record template.
loop.output: A structured draft distinguishing applicant statements, documented facts, and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Link statements to notes, preserve uncertainty, validate numbers, and require interviewer approval before filing.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, capped at 5,000 input words; unclear notes or unresolved facts return to manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Direct mappings handle form fields; variable typed explanations need bounded drafting into a consistent record.

steps.what: Send the applicant a missing-evidence checklist through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure the {WORKFLOW} to build an interview agenda from missing application fields, arrange appointments through the {CALENDAR}, and send preparation checklists through the {EMAIL}. The clerk conducts the conversation, then a bounded drafting loop turns typed notes into a verified record in the {DOCS}; routine evidence requests use approved fields and templates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation and paperwork were treated as inseparable from the interview. Notes varied between interviewers, while scheduling and follow-up required separate manual actions.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, scheduling flows, and checklist rules are established capabilities. A small drafting loop can structure typed notes while keeping factual verification with the interviewer.
tasks.still_hard: Applicants may misunderstand questions, lack documents, or need sensitive explanations and accessible support. GDPR requires proportionate collection and controlled processing; recording or employee monitoring would add consultation questions under national rules, and creditworthiness automation would require EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, ask proportionate follow-up questions, recognise misunderstanding, and let applicants explain circumstances in their own words.
tasks.altitude: The clerk has more time for clarification and assisted completion, with less scheduling and note formatting. Authority over credit decisions does not change.

reach.task: Help an applicant understand evidence requirements before an interview.
reach.learn: Explain document requirements accessibly, protect financial information, and escalate questions requiring credit judgment.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, missing-field checklists, and template notifications can use existing workflow configuration.
Drafting structured records from typed notes is a bounded model use; credit-interview accuracy and savings are not demonstrated by the digest.
The NBER study found productivity gains for assisted support agents, providing adjacent evidence rather than a credit-interview outcome estimate.

assumptions: The telephone route is shown; in-person interviews retain the same preparation and recordkeeping changes.
The baseline uses typed notes and does not require call recording.
The preparation pack lets applicants review known fields and identify missing documents without requiring self-service completion.
Routine notifications contain approved requests and no credit acceptance, rejection, or new assessment.
Conversation time falls only modestly because clarification remains central.
unknowns: How many interviews occur by telephone, in person, or with accessibility support?
Which questions and identity checks are mandatory?
Are applications structured enough to generate a reliable missing-data agenda?
Can typed notes be processed in the permitted environment?
Who approves interview records and handles disputed statements?
What access and employee consultation requirements apply under national rules?
research_questions: Which questions can disappear because reliable answers already exist in the application?
Can applicants use the preparation pack without digital access or specialist financial knowledge?
Does drafting preserve qualifications and distinguish applicant statements from verified evidence?
Do interviewers detect omissions during realistic record-review exercises?
new_work: Review draft interview records and correct unsupported statements.
Maintain question lists, accessible preparation materials, and evidence templates.
Handle scheduling exceptions and applicants needing assisted completion.
Monitor drafting quality, processing permissions, and record retention.
tasks.statement: Interview credit applicants by telephone or in person to obtain personal and financial data needed to complete credit report.

tasks.short: Assess payment history and credit records, then approve or decline new credit within delegated limits.

steps.what: Retrieve the customer's balance, overdue invoices and payment history from the {ERP}.
Retrieve the credit report through the {OTHER} credit-reference service.
Compare exposure and payment behaviour against credit policy in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Review evidence and decide approval, refusal or escalation within delegated credit authority.
Record the approved decision, reasons and account limit in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: A rules service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines {ERP} history with structured reports from the {OTHER} credit-reference service and produces an evidence-linked assessment. The credit officer makes a meaningful decision through the {WORKFLOW}; only that approved decision updates the {ERP}, with reasons and an audit trail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate credit-reference access, inconsistent customer identifiers and local policy calculations made integration costly. Existing approval controls also discouraged unattended account changes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces and configurable approvals can handle much of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mappings, calculations and validation; no model judgement is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Report licensing, stale data, disputed debts and policy exceptions remain difficult. GDPR decision safeguards and EU AI Act classification need assessment; a human signature alone does not establish meaningful review.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when apparently poor payment history reflects a genuine dispute or temporary difficulty, and justify a proportionate decision.

ambition.what: Weekly review of accounts approaching their approved credit limit.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling records to examining disputed and borderline cases. Evidence preparation creates capacity for weekly limit reviews; any wider credit authority still requires explicit delegation.

reach.task: Explain a credit hold and the available review route.
reach.learn: Translate decision reasons into plain language without promising approval or exposing restricted credit data.

evidence.claim: Structured financial calculations and policy comparisons can use deterministic code; these estimates are unvalidated.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
A score strongly relied on by a lender can itself constitute automated decision-making.
Creditworthiness AI can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk categories; applicability requires assessment.

assumptions: The baseline is a mid-size company's customer-account credit team, mainly handling trade credit.
Core payment and credit-reference fields are structured; document-heavy financial analysis is outside this task.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
Access work includes data protection review and employee consultation where national rules require it.
The meaningful human decision explains why automation is lower than the supplied near-total-automation prior.
unknowns: Whether applicants are businesses, individuals or both.
Available interfaces, credit-reference licences and customer identifier quality.
Actual policy thresholds, delegation limits and exception volumes.
Whether consumer-credit requirements apply to the company's offering.
Existing employee consultation arrangements and approval authority.
research_questions: Can historical cases reproduce approved policy calculations without changing decision outcomes?
Does the approval screen support independent consideration, overrides and recorded reasons?
Which GDPR safeguards and EU AI Act obligations apply to the proposed implementation?
new_work: Maintain versioned credit rules and report mappings.
Investigate missing, stale or conflicting financial records.
Review calculation drift and approval overrides.
Handle correction requests and challenges to credit decisions.
tasks.statement: Evaluate customers' computerized credit records and payment histories to decide whether to approve new credit, based on predetermined standards.

tasks.short: Match sales slips to customer accounts and retain billing evidence.

steps.what: Collect digital sales slips from the {DOCS} billing folder.
Match each slip to its customer account and transaction in the {ERP}.
Attach a separate slip copy to the customer ledger in the {ERP}.
Check filing totals and resolve unmatched slips before billing.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to retain one authoritative sales document and link it to both the transaction and customer ledger. A deterministic connector links documents from the {DOCS}, checks identifiers and totals, and sends ambiguous matches to the {WORKFLOW} for approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sales documents and ledger records arrived through separate channels. Clerks compensated for weak identifiers and inconvenient document links by copying files.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document links and import features can remove duplicate filing. Small connectors and reconciliation checks are now cheaper to build and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Unreadable legacy slips, reused transaction references and split transactions need investigation. Retention, access controls and historical migration can cost more than the matching logic.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous ownership of a transaction and recognise evidence that should not be attached to a customer's account.
tasks.altitude: Routine filing largely disappears, leaving a short exception queue and periodic reconciliation. Credit or billing decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Retrieve supporting sales evidence for a billing dispute.
reach.learn: Follow transaction references and distinguish the authoritative document from a duplicate.

evidence.claim: Existing software imports orders and synchronises stock; this supports source-record integration, not proof of slip filing.
Document capture software validates order data and routes exceptions; credit-ledger attachment requires separate validation.
Exact identifier matching, duplicate prevention and batch reconciliation need no model.

assumptions: Sales slips usually arrive digitally or have already been scanned.
Most slips carry a stable transaction reference; free-text extraction is not the main workload.
The target retains a durable source document with ledger access, allowing separate copies to disappear.
Shares include time spent on exceptions across the caseload.
Build estimates exclude bulk historical migration; access work includes consultation if national rules require it.
unknowns: The proportion of physical, scanned and structured sales slips.
Whether the existing ledger supports durable document links.
Reference quality, duplicate rates and transaction splitting frequency.
Required retention periods and access restrictions.
Whether automatic source-to-ledger linking already exists but is unused.
research_questions: Can existing configuration eliminate the separate filing queue entirely?
Which exact matching keys avoid cross-customer attachments?
Can reconciliation detect missing documents and failed links before billing?
new_work: Resolve unmatched and conflicting references.
Monitor failed imports and broken document links.
Maintain document retention and access settings.
Sample automatic matches after source-format changes.
tasks.statement: File sales slips in customers' ledgers for billing purposes.

tasks.short: Receive credit applications and charge slips, clarify missing details, and register complete cases.

steps.what: Receive applications and scanned postal charge slips in the shared {EMAIL} inbox.
Read application attachments in the {DOCS} and note the supplied financial details.

loop.input: Application attachments and a fixed field schema.
loop.output: Draft application details with source locations and explicit missing fields.
loop.check: Validate types, dates and totals; require source evidence for each field and human confirmation of material financial values.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per bundle; unreadable or conflicting fields go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Variable document layouts and narrative financial details exceed fixed-field parsing; structured forms bypass the loop.

steps.what: Take merchant calls or clarify application details by telephone.
Check required application fields and account identifiers in the {ERP}.
Request missing application information through {EMAIL}.
Register the complete application and supporting documents in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Configure a structured intake form in the {WORKFLOW} and capture existing {EMAIL} submissions into the same queue. A bounded extraction loop prepares document fields for review, while fixed checks request missing information and register complete cases in the {ERP}. Clerks retain assisted telephone intake, supported by a prefilled checklist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mixed documents and telephone submissions resisted a single import format. Re-keying and repeated requests were easier than maintaining many document templates.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured forms remove much of the variation. Bounded extraction can draft fields from remaining documents, with deterministic validation and targeted review.
tasks.still_hard: Unreadable documents, identity discrepancies and sensitive financial explanations remain costly. Physical post still needs opening and scanning; no capture tool establishes creditworthiness.
tasks.human_edge: Help an applicant explain an unusual situation, clarify ambiguous answers and spot inconsistencies that require investigation.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time copying fields and chasing omissions, creating room for booked assistance. Intake staff can resolve completeness issues within a checklist; credit approval authority does not expand.

reach.task: Route a caller to a suitable assisted application appointment.
reach.learn: Recognise intake needs, verify contact details and avoid collecting unnecessary financial information.

evidence.claim: Document capture products read order documents, validate data and route exceptions; application extraction is an adaptation.
Existing request software can turn an unresolved interaction into a prefilled request.
The proposed extraction accuracy, review effort and build ranges require local validation.

assumptions: The shared mailroom scans physical post before this team's intake work begins.
Telephone work includes direct submissions and follow-up clarification; not every case uses every channel.
Time shares describe the mixed caseload and give the shared mailbox more weight than the weak mail prior.
Automatic requests use fixed templates, verified contacts and a secure return route.
No call recording or automated credit assessment is introduced; consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Actual intake channels, document languages and postal volumes.
Whether applicants can use a secure form and return documents securely.
Required fields and permitted identity checks.
Availability of verified contact details.
Whether assisted appointments already exist and whether demand supports them.
research_questions: Which fields can move to a structured form without excluding applicants?
Can extraction preserve exact financial values and clearly abstain on uncertain fields?
Which missing-information requests can safely use fixed templates?
Does preparation reduce call administration while preserving useful conversation?
new_work: Review extracted material fields and conflicting evidence.
Maintain intake requirements, templates and document test samples.
Resolve duplicate applications and failed registrations.
Manage assisted appointment capacity and accessibility feedback.
tasks.statement: Receive charge slips or credit applications by mail, or receive information from salespeople or merchants by telephone.

tasks.short: Prepare customer charge statements, release delivery batches, and handle failed delivery.

steps.what: Select customer accounts due for statements in the {ERP}.
Generate customer charge statements in the {ERP}.
Check balances, delivery details and holds, then approve the statement batch.
Send electronic statements through {EMAIL}.
Print statements using the {OTHER} printing system, then envelope and post them.
Investigate bounced messages and returned post received through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled statement generation and fixed balance, address and hold checks in the {ERP}; the {WORKFLOW} presents exceptions and a batch release. Once released, delivery uses {EMAIL} or an integrated {OTHER} print-and-mail service, with delivery failures returned to a single queue. Verified corrections trigger controlled resends with duplicate-send protection.
tasks.previous_blocker: Delivery preferences, account holds and postal handling sat outside the statement run. Manual batch checks bridged these gaps.
tasks.enabler_now: Most statement generation and scheduled delivery can use existing configuration. Small integrations can join approval, postal fulfilment and delivery status without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Outdated addresses, disputed balances and postal fulfilment remain operational problems. A statement sent to the wrong recipient cannot be recalled, so recipient mapping needs strong validation.
tasks.human_edge: Judge when a dispute or vulnerable customer's circumstances call for a hold, explanation or specialist follow-up.
tasks.altitude: Batch preparation shrinks to exception review and release, with time left for failed-delivery cases. Authority over credit terms and disputed balances does not change.

reach.task: Prepare a clear response to a disputed statement.
reach.learn: Trace ledger entries, explain corrections and recognise when a reply needs credit-team approval.

evidence.claim: Scheduled statement generation, fixed checks and template delivery are standard deterministic capabilities; local coverage varies.
Integrated postal fulfilment can remove clerk handling, but physical delivery and its charges remain.

assumptions: The typical caseload uses electronic statements with a smaller postal segment.
The ledger already produces valid statements; the change does not redesign accounting or collection policy.
Batch approval authorises the downstream sends; delivery steps do not need repeated approval.
A suitable print-and-mail service is available; otherwise postal preparation remains manual.
Delivery failures from physical post are logged into the shared queue.
Access work includes delivery-provider data protection review and consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Existing statement scheduling and delivery features.
Electronic delivery preferences and postal volumes.
Who can release batches, change addresses and clear billing holds.
Availability and terms of a print-and-mail service.
Actual bounce, return and incorrect-recipient rates.

Do batch checks detect cross-customer attachments, held accounts and stale addresses?
Can retries and resends avoid duplicate delivery?
Which postal accounts can move to electronic delivery under applicable requirements and customer preferences?

Investigate delivery failures and verify address corrections.
Maintain templates, schedules and delivery preferences.
Monitor provider failures, duplicate prevention and delivery charges.

tasks.short: Verify relevant public records and resolve identity matches before using findings in a credit assessment.

steps.what: Open the application in the {OTHER} credit account system and establish permitted checks.
Search permitted registers through the {GOV_PORTAL} and licensed sources through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Read register extracts in the {DOCS} and capture relevant dates, identifiers and findings.

loop.input: Permitted register extracts and a fixed finding schema.
loop.output: Finding table with source passages, dates and identifiers.
loop.check: Validate field types and source references; require review of adverse findings and uncertain extraction.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; unreadable or unsupported documents go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use structured fields first; variable document layouts and narrative entries need bounded extraction.

steps.what: Compare identifiers and addresses against the application to resolve possible identity matches.
Decide which verified findings are relevant and require clarification before credit assessment.
Attach verified findings and source references to the {OTHER} credit account system.

tasks.design: Configure permitted checks in the {WORKFLOW}, remove redundant directory searches, and retrieve authorised records through supported {GOV_PORTAL} and {PARTNER_PORTAL} interfaces. A bounded extractor prepares source-linked findings in the {DOCS}; the clerk resolves identity ambiguity and relevance before an integration attaches verified evidence to the {OTHER} credit account system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Register access, inconsistent identifiers and document formats made retrieval and checking expensive. These constraints still exist.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding shortens connector and validation work. Bounded extraction can reduce reading time where structured register data is unavailable.
tasks.still_hard: Licensed access, stale records, disputed identities and permitted use remain difficult. Public availability alone does not justify collecting or using a record.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a mistaken identity, distinguish an unresolved allegation from a reliable finding, and seek a fair clarification.

ambition.what: Source-linked correction pack for applicants disputing a public-record match.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching and copying, and more time resolving disputed matches. Within an agreed mandate, the clerk can mark evidence unusable pending clarification; credit approval authority does not expand.

reach.learn: Identity verification, correction routes and how to explain source limitations without disclosing unrelated records.

evidence.claim: Structured retrieval, exact identifier checks and source logging are deterministic engineering patterns, not a documented credit deployment here.
Rossum demonstrates document capture, validation and exception routing for orders; transfer to credit records requires separate validation.
The SCHUFA judgment shows that a score strongly relied upon by a lender can itself constitute an automated decision.

assumptions: The European baseline is relevant address, business, ownership or insolvency verification where permitted. Arrest-record searches are excluded unless a specific lawful and necessary use is established.
Supported register access is assumed for automated retrieval; inaccessible sources retain manual retrieval.
Credit assessment and approval occur downstream. This solution does not calculate creditworthiness or make adverse decisions.
GDPR applies throughout. Adding AI creditworthiness assessment requires separate EU AI Act classification and applicable-date review.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates informed by the priors, not measured savings.
Build ranges are working-day estimates. Access, privacy review and employee consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time.

Which purposes, permissions and source licences support each check?
Which sources offer authorised structured access?
How often do ambiguous identities or disputed findings occur?
Which employee consultation requirements apply?

What restrictions apply to criminal-offence data and credit-related public records in the relevant jurisdictions?
Which downstream uses could turn evidence preparation into regulated automated credit assessment?

Handle unavailable sources and disputed identities.
Maintain permitted-source rules, retention settings and connectors.
Sample source accuracy and track correction outcomes.
tasks.statement: Examine city directories and public records to verify residence property ownership, bankruptcies, liens, arrest record, or unpaid taxes of applicants.

tasks.short: Provide authorised subscribers with credit report information and explain its contents.

steps.what: Check subscriber identity, entitlement and permitted purpose in the {CRM}.
Retrieve the current report from the {PARTNER_PORTAL} or the {OTHER} credit reporting system.
Prepare a permitted report extract and covering explanation using templates in the {DOCS}.
Check recipient and permitted content, then release the report through the {EMAIL}.
Explain requested report information to the authenticated subscriber through the {TELEPHONY}.
Record the recipient, report version and disclosure outcome in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Connect subscriber entitlements in the {CRM} to report retrieval through the {PARTNER_PORTAL} or the {OTHER} credit reporting system. Deterministic templates produce permitted extracts and a secure delivery link, with clerk approval before release through the {EMAIL}; delivery metadata and a structured call outcome populate the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Subscriber permissions, report versions and delivery records sat in separate places. Staff manually checked each disclosure and copied details.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing access controls, templates and delivery workflows can handle much of the work. AI coding reduces the effort of connecting them; a model is unnecessary for standard reports.
tasks.still_hard: Establishing entitlement, licensing onward disclosure and explaining contested or ambiguous information still require care.
tasks.human_edge: Explain what a report establishes, acknowledge uncertainty and recognise when the subscriber needs a correction or specialist assessment.
tasks.altitude: The clerk handles fewer retrieval and formatting chores and has more time for report explanations. The clerk can resolve delivery problems within policy; disclosure rights and credit decision authority do not expand.

reach.task: Prepare a clear response to a report-correction request.
reach.learn: Plain-language explanations, source attribution and permitted disclosure boundaries.

evidence.claim: Entitlement checks, field-based extracts, templated delivery and disclosure logs can use deterministic software.
TOPdesk Robin demonstrates knowledge-based answering and pre-filled handover, but does not establish safe credit-report disclosure.
GDPR automated-decision safeguards matter if report communication expands into decision-making.

assumptions: Subscriber reporting applies to a credit-information service or an organisation with authorised onward disclosure; it is not universal mid-size company work.
Today's service uses email or post and telephone. Shares represent the blended channel mix, not a requirement to use every channel per request.
Automated entitlement checks accept only established identities, current permissions and explicit purposes; uncertain requests enter an exception queue.
A secure report link replaces attachments or post where permitted. Postal exceptions remain manual.
The clerk explains report content without making an automated credit decision.
GDPR applies; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
Build ranges and time reductions are estimates. Consultation and external access approval may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Does the organisation provide reports to subscribers, and under which licence?
What proportion of requests arrive by telephone, post or email?
Which report fields may each subscriber receive?
Can delivery status and structured call outcomes be captured automatically?
research_questions: Which source licences allow extracts, secure links and explanatory templates?
Which identity checks are proportionate for each delivery channel?
new_work: Resolve failed authentication and entitlement exceptions.
Review recipient and report content before release.
Maintain disclosure templates, permissions and delivery rules.
Handle expired links, correction requests and failed deliveries.
tasks.statement: Relay credit report information to subscribers by mail or by telephone.

tasks.short: Prepare and issue approved account cards through an authorised card programme.

steps.what: Retrieve approved issuance instructions from the {OTHER} credit account system.
Check cardholder details and delivery address against the {CRM}.
Enter personalisation details and inspect the production proof in the {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Approve the production proof and submit the issuance order through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Receive the physical cards and check quantities and personalisation against the production order.
Package checked cards for authorised delivery and record dispatch in the {OTHER} issuance system.

tasks.design: Connect approved accounts in the {OTHER} credit account system and verified details in the {CRM} to deterministic card templates and the {PARTNER_PORTAL}. The clerk approves the production order, while configured workflows track receipt, discrepancies and dispatch; physical handling remains where local fulfilment is required.
tasks.previous_blocker: Provider-specific file formats and disconnected customer records encouraged rekeying. Physical production and secure fulfilment were never software-only tasks.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing issuance templates and supported provider interfaces can automate preparation. AI coding can speed up adapters and validation without introducing a model.
tasks.still_hard: Provider certification, secure personalisation, replacements and physical custody remain costly. A mid-size employer cannot assume it controls the issuer's process.
tasks.human_edge: Notice suspicious issuance requests, incorrect personalisation or custody failures and stop release before a customer is affected.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time rekeying and more time handling issuance exceptions and physical checks. Credit limits, issuer responsibilities and approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve a missing or incorrectly personalised card enquiry.
reach.learn: Secure identity checks, replacement procedures and how to interpret issuance status.

evidence.claim: Field validation, template personalisation and issuance-order transfer are deterministic patterns; the digest provides no card-issuance deployment.
Physical card inspection and local fulfilment require operational work unless an authorised provider takes them over.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies only where the organisation operates an authorised account-card programme.
The baseline uses an external producer and local receipt and dispatch. Direct provider fulfilment would remove the local physical steps.
Legacy embossed charge plates are uncommon; obsolete plate preparation should be eliminated where the account process permits.
Issuance follows an existing approved account decision and does not grant new credit.
Sensitive card credentials remain within the authorised provider's controls.
GDPR applies. National rules determine any required employee consultation.
Build ranges are estimates; provider onboarding, certification and access approval can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Are physical cards or charge plates actually prepared?
Who is the authorised issuer and production provider?
Does the provider support bulk files or an authorised interface?
Are cards dispatched locally or directly by the provider?
Which production and release checks are mandatory?
research_questions: Can existing provider configuration remove rekeying before building an adapter?
Can legacy plates or local fulfilment be removed without changing customer access?
new_work: Review production proofs and release orders.
Resolve rejected files, duplicate requests and provider outages.
Maintain templates and field mappings.
Reconcile production, receipt, replacement and dispatch records.
tasks.statement: Prepare credit cards or charge account plates.

tasks.short: Contact customers about overdue balances, resolve disputes and agree permitted payment arrangements.

steps.what: Select overdue accounts from the ageing view in the {ERP}.
Check recent receipts, disputed invoices and existing payment arrangements across the {ERP} and {CRM}.
Prepare a call brief and permitted arrangement options from the {CRM} and {DOCS}.
Call the customer, verify identity, discuss non-payment and agree options within delegated authority.
Review arrangements outside the clerk's mandate and approve or return them through the {CRM}.
Record the call outcome, agreed terms and follow-up date in the {CRM}.

loop.input: Clerk-entered call notes and any required supervisor decision.
loop.output: Draft outcome, explicit payment commitments and follow-up date.
loop.check: Validate dates, amounts and policy limits; the clerk confirms agreement and approval before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per call; ambiguous commitments require manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields handle standard calls; free-text notes need extraction for nonstandard outcomes.

steps.what: Send the customer a written confirmation of agreed terms through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure an overdue queue in the {ERP} and join receipts, disputes and arrangements from the {CRM} before preparing a deterministic call brief. People conduct calls and approve exceptional terms; a bounded note extractor prepares the collection record for clerk approval, and templates produce the confirmation through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payment updates, disputes and contact history were fragmented. Negotiation also depends on circumstances that cannot be reduced to a payment schedule.
tasks.enabler_now: Integrations and existing queue configuration can remove preparation work. A small extraction loop can turn clerk notes into reviewed records without automating the conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Late payment allocation, genuine disputes, financial distress and arrangements outside policy still need people. Reliable suppression of inappropriate calls depends on current source data.
tasks.human_edge: Listen without pressuring, distinguish inability to pay from an invoice dispute, and negotiate a credible next step.

ambition.what: Daily review of broken payment promises.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling balances and writing notes, leaving more time for difficult calls and dispute resolution. Within a delegated mandate, the clerk can pause collection contact and route a dispute; exceptional concessions still need approval.

reach.task: Resolve the invoice or service dispute blocking payment.
reach.learn: Invoice evidence, dispute categorisation and how to close the loop with the collection clerk.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of office and administrative support workers
reach.task: Review collection workload and exceptional payment arrangements.
reach.learn: Queue ageing, approval limits and outcome measures that do not reward pressure on customers.

evidence.claim: Ageing queues, balance reconciliation, arrangement calculations and templated confirmations suit deterministic software.
A study of 5,179 support agents found improved issues resolved per hour with an assistant; it does not establish debt-collection outcomes.
The digest identifies emotion recognition on agents as prohibited; it is excluded from this design.

assumptions: The baseline is collection of existing overdue customer balances, not legal enforcement or new lending.
Supervisor review is an exception branch; its share is averaged over the case mix.
Recent payments, active disputes and contact restrictions suppress queue entries; stale data routes a case for checking.
Call preparation includes current balances and explicit policy options, not inferred vulnerability or behavioural scoring.
The note loop uses clerk-entered notes. Call recording is unnecessary for the proposed design.
GDPR applies, and national rules govern collection conduct and applicable employee consultation.
A chatbot or automated creditworthiness assessment would require a separate EU AI Act review.
Build ranges and time reductions are estimates; consultation and access approval can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Are customers consumers, businesses or both?
How quickly are receipts and disputes reflected in the source records?
Which arrangements can the clerk agree without supervisor approval?
Which contact limits and hardship procedures apply?
Can standard outcomes be captured through existing structured fields?
Does the proposed workflow change require employee consultation?
research_questions: Which national collection rules affect contact timing, arrangements and dispute handling?
Can existing structured outcome forms remove enough note work to avoid the extraction loop?
What reconciliation checks reliably prevent contact after payment or dispute registration?
new_work: Resolve stale balances, unallocated receipts and suppression failures.
Review extracted commitments and customer confirmations.
Maintain arrangement limits, queue rules and templates.
Monitor broken promises, unresolved disputes and inappropriate contacts.
tasks.statement: Call customers to collect payment on delinquent accounts.

tasks.short: Resolve customer complaints and verify disputed financial or credit transactions.

steps.what: Read the complaint and identify the customer account.
Retrieve invoices, payments, account limits and earlier correspondence.
Ask the customer to confirm disputed details and supply missing evidence.
Assess the complaint and choose a resolution within delegated limits.
Approve and post the proposed account correction.
Write the case note and attach supporting evidence.

loop.input: Clerk notes, posted resolution and linked transaction evidence.
loop.output: Draft case note with evidence references.
loop.check: Validate account and transaction identifiers; clerk checks disputed facts and omissions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence returns the note to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer explanations vary; templates alone lose relevant context.

steps.what: Send the customer a written confirmation of the resolution.

tasks.design: An integration assembles a transaction pack from the {ERP}, {CRM} and {HELPDESK}, with account matching and freshness checks. The clerk conducts the conversation; configured approvals control account corrections, while a bounded drafting loop prepares the case note and templates prepare the confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence sits across account screens and correspondence. Complaint handling also mixes retrieval with negotiation and financial authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case workflows and account interfaces can support the process. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and building evidence-linked drafting.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting evidence, disputed identity and negotiated remedies need people. Account corrections require reliable permissions and protection against duplicate posting.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise distress, test conflicting explanations and negotiate a fair remedy within delegated authority.

ambition.what: A customer explanation showing how a disputed balance was reconstructed.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling records and more time resolving difficult complaints. Financial approval limits remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Explain payment allocation and recognise complaints that require credit authority.

evidence.claim: Configured support systems can retrieve records and perform integrated actions; this supports the case-workflow pattern, not credit decision automation.
Evidence retrieval, template confirmations and approval routing can use deterministic technology.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.

assumptions: The baseline is customer account support in a mid-size European company.
Time shares are estimates of today's work, not measured savings.
A read-only export version can provide preparation before write access is available.
No call recording or employee performance monitoring is introduced.
Access estimates include consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Available account and case interfaces.
Delegated correction and refund limits.
Actual complaint channels, volumes and handling times.
Existing customer verification procedures.
research_questions: Which account actions have legal or similarly significant effects in this service?
Which national complaint-handling and record-retention rules apply?
new_work: Review draft case notes and confirmations.
Resolve account-matching and stale-record exceptions.
Maintain resolution templates and approval routing.
Check failed or duplicate account updates.
tasks.statement: Consult with customers to resolve complaints or verify financial or credit transactions.

tasks.short: Verify relevant employment or reference details when credit evidence is incomplete.

steps.what: Check whether third-party verification is necessary and permitted.
Find reliable contact details and check existing evidence.
Send a limited verification request to the confirmed contact.
Discuss permitted factual questions with the reference contact.
Compare the response with application evidence and flag unresolved differences.
Record the finding, evidence source and unresolved questions.

tasks.design: A configured form in the {WORKFLOW} uses an approved verification scope, reuses existing evidence from the {DOCS} and prepares a minimal request through the {EMAIL}. Structured findings return to the {CRM}; an evidence-sufficiency rule removes unnecessary third-party contacts, while people handle necessary conversations and contradictions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verification depends on external contacts and inconsistent evidence. The original occupational wording also mixes useful factual checks with intrusive enquiries.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, templates and retention controls already exist in standard software. AI-assisted coding makes a small evidence checklist and record integration cheaper to assemble.
tasks.still_hard: Contact authenticity, relevance and lawful disclosure cannot be inferred from a completed form. Health information requires a separate legal basis and special-category condition.
tasks.human_edge: Question inconsistencies without treating hearsay, silence or an unhelpful reference as proof against the applicant.
tasks.altitude: The clerk makes fewer unnecessary contacts and spends more time resolving material evidence gaps. Credit approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare requests for missing applicant evidence.
reach.learn: Write minimal factual requests and distinguish a missing fact from adverse evidence.

evidence.claim: Structured requests, evidence checklists and record updates can be configured without a model.
Routine enquiries about health or social behaviour are not assumed typical or necessary for European credit processing.
GDPR requires purpose limitation and data minimisation; health data also needs an applicable special-category condition.

assumptions: This is an occasional verification task, not routine background investigation.
The baseline uses employment or business-reference facts relevant to the application.
Health history and social gossip are excluded from the proposed process.
Adequate existing evidence can remove the need for a reference contact.
Access estimates include legal review and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether this company performs third-party reference checks at all.
Which facts its verification policy permits.
Accepted alternatives to employer confirmation.
Current retention periods and approved contact channels.
research_questions: What lawful basis supports each proposed third-party enquiry?
Which national rules restrict employer disclosures or credit-reference enquiries?
When can applicant-provided evidence replace a third-party contact?
new_work: Maintain permitted question sets and evidence-sufficiency rules.
Review contact authenticity and disclosure scope.
Handle unanswered requests and disputed findings.
Apply retention limits to reference evidence.
tasks.statement: Contact former employers and other acquaintances to verify applicants' references, employment, health history, or social behavior.

tasks.short: Prepare evidence-backed credit findings and recommendations for an authorized decision-maker.

steps.what: Collect the application, account history and verification findings.
Calculate exposure and payment indicators in the reporting workbook.
Assess evidence gaps and formulate a recommendation against credit policy.
Write the findings report with supporting evidence and caveats.

loop.input: Validated metrics, cited evidence and the clerk's explicit recommendation.
loop.output: Draft narrative within a fixed report template.
loop.check: Insert numbers deterministically; require evidence references; reject unsupported claims or changed recommendations.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; unresolved checks return the narrative to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover fixed sections, but varied evidence needs concise explanatory prose.

steps.what: Review the report and release the approved version to the case.

tasks.design: A deterministic job assembles evidence from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {DOCS}, calculates metrics and fills a report template. A bounded loop drafts narrative around the clerk's recommendation; approval in the {WORKFLOW} releases a versioned report without changing account limits.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence assembly and workbook calculations are separated from report writing. Recommendations and factual narration are often written together.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable calculations and templates can be coded quickly, while bounded drafting can turn approved findings into readable prose. Neither requires autonomous investigation.
tasks.still_hard: Source evidence may be incomplete or contradictory. A polished report can obscure uncertainty unless reviewers inspect the underlying evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether evidence supports a recommendation and explain the uncertainty that matters to the decision.

ambition.what: A credit decision evidence brief with traceable reasons and unresolved questions.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time calculating and formatting, and more time testing recommendations. The authorized decision-maker retains credit approval rights.

reach.task: Review difficult credit cases and coach report writers.
reach.learn: Evaluate evidence quality, challenge recommendations and explain policy exceptions.

evidence.claim: Calculations, evidence assembly and fixed report sections can use deterministic code; variable narrative can use bounded drafting.
A credit score strongly relied on by a lender can itself count as automated decision-making; a nominal human review is insufficient.
AI used to evaluate natural persons' creditworthiness is listed as high-risk, subject to the applicable scope and exceptions.

assumptions: The clerk currently uses a workbook to calculate indicators; companies with equivalent reports in the {ERP} should configure those first.
The model does not score applicants or invent recommendations.
Report approval does not authorize a credit limit or rejection.
Build estimates cover report preparation, not a new credit assessment model.
Access estimates include consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Existing report templates and calculation definitions.
Whether equivalent reports already exist in the {ERP}.
Required evidence provenance and approval records.
Whether cases concern natural persons, companies or both.
research_questions: Does the intended use remain clerical report preparation under the EU AI Act?
What constitutes meaningful human review in the actual credit decision process?
Which consumer-credit explanation and intervention requirements apply at rollout?
new_work: Review drafted narrative against source evidence.
Maintain calculation definitions and report templates.
Test that drafting preserves recommendations and uncertainty.
Monitor missing evidence and failed data refreshes.
tasks.statement: Prepare reports of findings and recommendations.

tasks.short: Identify overdue accounts and select suitable cases for collection.

steps.what: Run the receivables ageing report for the review date.
Reconcile recent receipts, credit notes and payment allocations.
Check disputes, payment arrangements and other reasons to pause collection.
Apply collection criteria and prepare the proposed account list.
Review exceptions and approve accounts for the internal collection queue.
Enter approved accounts into the collection queue with supporting records.

tasks.design: Configure ageing, eligibility rules and the internal collection queue in the {ERP}; connect current receipts from the {BANK} and hold statuses from the {CRM} and {HELPDESK}. Missing or stale evidence creates an exception, and supervisor approval binds the selected accounts and balances before an idempotent queue update.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ageing is already available, but receipts and dispute status arrive through separate systems. A workbook often bridges the review and the collection queue.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing receivables functions can handle most rules. Small integrations can now be built faster to supply current holds and receipts.
tasks.still_hard: Unallocated payments, disputed debts and undocumented arrangements remain difficult. Reliable hold capture matters more than more elaborate scoring.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an overdue balance is unsuitable for collection and resolve ambiguity before escalation.

ambition.what: A daily review of newly overdue accounts that have complete receipt and hold evidence.

tasks.altitude: The clerk works through payment and dispute exceptions instead of rebuilding lists. The supervisor retains referral approval, and external collection actions require their own authorization.

reach.task: Capture invoice disputes before collection review.
reach.learn: Record a clear dispute reason, affected invoice and next review date.

evidence.claim: Receivables ageing, fixed collection criteria and internal queue creation can use existing configuration and deterministic integrations.
A structured internal work queue differs from an automated external collection action; later significant actions need separate assessment.
GDPR Article 22 applies where automated processing alone produces legal or similarly significant effects.

assumptions: The task ends at an internal collection queue.
No automatic customer demand, agency referral or legal filing is included.
Unresolved payments and possible holds block automatic inclusion.
Structured hold fields are introduced where current notes are insufficient.
Build estimates assume the {ERP} exposes usable receivables configuration.
Access estimates include consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Current ageing and collection configuration in the {ERP}.
Receipt posting delays and unallocated payment volumes.
How disputes and payment arrangements are currently recorded.
Required approval thresholds and review frequency.
research_questions: Which national rules govern consumer and commercial collection referral?
When would queue selection itself have a significant effect on a natural person?
What freshness checks are sufficient before a later external collection action?
new_work: Resolve unmatched payments and missing hold information.
Maintain collection thresholds and hold categories.
Review approved lists when balances change before queue entry.
Monitor duplicate prevention and integration failures.
tasks.statement: Review individual or commercial customer files to identify and select delinquent accounts for collection.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward evidence quality, allocation exceptions, careful applicant conversations, and defensible credit analysis. Credit decisions and sensitive disclosures retain explicit human authority; automation alone grants no additional decision rights.
reach: Customer service representatives: explain payment status and application evidence requirements.
Correspondence clerks: prepare controlled factual references and correction acknowledgements.
First-line administrative supervisors: triage evidence bottlenecks and coordinate exception handling.
skills_to_grow: Configure matching rules, forms, templates, and exception queues.
Read financial indicators and trace them to source evidence.
Review extracted facts and drafted records without rubber-stamping.
Apply GDPR safeguards, disclosure permissions, and relevant national rules.
Conduct accessible interviews and explain uncertainty clearly.
Monitor integration failures and maintain auditable records.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide an applicant evidence service that combines preparation checklists, correction tracking, and clear explanations of missing information. Credit analysts retain assessment authority, while clerks gain a defined coordination role across applicants, finance, and external reference providers.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward credit exceptions, meaningful approval, assisted intake and billing disputes. Faster preparation supports more frequent account reviews; additional financial authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Customer service representatives: explain credit holds and organise review requests.
Correspondence clerks: prepare evidence-based responses to statement disputes.
Receptionists: route applicants to assisted intake without gathering unnecessary financial data.
skills_to_grow: Interpret credit policy and explain defensible decisions.
Validate financial records and trace source evidence.
Review exceptions without rubber-stamping calculated results.
Configure field checks, approval routes and reconciliation controls.
Understand GDPR safeguards, applicable EU AI Act duties and relevant national rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A credit operations specialist who runs a weekly near-limit account review and scheduled assisted intake, combining reliable records with proportionate human decisions.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts from retrieval, rekeying and paperwork toward evidence quality, clear explanations, disputed identities and payment conversations. Any expanded rights to pause contact or reject unreliable evidence need an explicit delegated mandate; credit approval authority does not automatically change.
reach: Customer service representative: resolve the underlying dispute and explain record corrections.
Correspondence clerk: produce clear, source-linked explanations and confirmations.
First-line supervisor of office and administrative support workers: review exceptions, workload and delegated arrangement limits.
skills_to_grow: Source provenance and identity-match checking.
Credit-report explanation and correction handling.
Payment negotiation and dispute triage.
Structured data validation and exception management.
Access controls, data minimisation and retention.
Testing templates, connectors and bounded extraction.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a coordinated credit-record correction and payment-resolution service, with people accountable for disputed evidence and consequential decisions. Reusable templates, schemas and validation code provide a head start across employers; customer data, licences and decision policies remain specific to each organisation.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward evidence quality, difficult customer conversations and justified exceptions. Credit limits, adverse decisions and external collection authority remain with their existing authorized roles.
reach: Help customer service representatives resolve invoice questions and capture actionable disputes.
Support correspondence clerks with minimal, accurate evidence requests.
Support first-line supervisors with traceable case briefs and exception analysis.
skills_to_grow: Payment reconciliation and evidence provenance.
Credit policy interpretation and delegated authority.
Complaint resolution and clear financial explanations.
Data minimisation and meaningful human review.
Configuring rules, testing exceptions and monitoring integrations.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide an evidence-led credit support service that reconstructs disputed balances, exposes missing facts and prepares explainable case briefs before an authorized person decides.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
